# Locality Guide — Tegucigalpa, Honduras (1870–1900)

## Jurisdictional Context

Tegucigalpa was the capital of the Department of Tegucigalpa from 1838 until 1943, when the department was renamed **Francisco Morazán**. Within the modern department the city sits in **Distrito Central**. For research purposes, records will appear under all three names depending on the collection and era. The city itself (`standardPlace`: Tegucigalpa, Distrito Central, Francisco Morazán, Honduras) has continuous records from 1536.

## Record Availability (1870–1900)

### 1. Civil Registration — PRIMARY SOURCE for 1881–1900

**Honduras, Civil Registration, 1841-1968** (FS col. 2135627) — 12.5 M records, 337,976 images. Index + images. Free on FamilySearch.

Key volumes for Tegucigalpa births 1887–1891 (Nacimientos):
- `M94G-38W` (Distrito Central, nov 1887–jul 1889, **100% indexed**, 245 images)
- `M94G-384` (Distrito Central, sept 1889–jun 1891, **100% indexed**, 234 images)
- `M94G-Y63` (Distrito Central, 1888–1891, **100% indexed**, 103 images)

All Spanish. Nacimientos (births) record child's name, date, parents' names, witnesses, and often legitimacy status.

Civil registration was officially instituted in Honduras in **1881**; earlier records (1841–1880) exist but are less complete.

### 2. Catholic Parish Records — PRIMARY SOURCE for pre-1881; SUPPLEMENT for 1881+

**Honduras, Catholic Church Records, 1633-1978** (FS col. 1823595) — 1.8 M records, 425,330 images. Index + images. Free on FamilySearch.

For Tegucigalpa (Catedral San Miguel Arcángel), FamilySearch has indexed baptismal volumes through **1878**. A gap in indexed/digitized Catholic baptismal images for Tegucigalpa cathedral from **1879 to the late 1880s** was detected in the volume survey. If a child was baptized at the cathedral in 1889 and does not appear in civil registration, browsing unindexed images in collection 1823595 filtered to Tegucigalpa is the next step.

**Honduras, Baptisms, 1730-1930** (FS col. 1520634) — 161,000 records. **Legacy/incomplete index only** — no new records added, no corrections made. Use as a lead pointer; always verify in original images.

### 3. Marriages

**Honduras, Marriages, 1800-1910** (FS col. 1520638) — 31,000 records. Index + images. Also available (index only) at Ancestry ($) and MyHeritage ($).

For civil marriage expedientes (supporting documents), separate volumes exist for Distrito Central 1882–1900, many full-text searchable: e.g. `M94G-CD6` (Expedientes matrimoniales, 1889, 331 images, full-text searchable).

### 4. External Repositories

- **Ancestry.com** (subscription): Honduras Select Baptisms 1730-1930 (col. 9889) and Select Marriages 1800-1910 (col. 9890) — partial indexes.
- **MyHeritage** (subscription): same indexes as Ancestry.
- **FindMyPast** (subscription): Honduras Baptism Index 1730-1930 and Marriage Index 1800-1910.
- **Registro Nacional de las Personas, Tegucigalpa** (+504 9775-2964): parish registers 1842–1881 (18 books) and direct contact for vital records.
- **Archivo Nacional, Tegucigalpa** (Av. Cristóbal Colón, tel. +504 222-8338): holds records from 1906 onward (approx. 2,176,000 pages).
- **WorldGenWeb Honduras**: https://www.worldgenweb.net/honduras — free research resources.

## Language and Script Notes

All records are in **Spanish** in 19th-century cursive handwriting. Key vocabulary: *Nacimiento* = birth; *Bautismo* = baptism; *Matrimonio* = marriage; *Defunción* = death; *Padre/Madre* = father/mother; *Padrino/Madrina* = godfather/godmother.

See the [Spanish Genealogical Word List](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Spanish_Genealogical_Word_List) and the [BYU Spanish Script Tutorial](https://script.byu.edu/spanish-handwriting/introduction) for reading assistance.

## Research Strategy for a Birth circa 1889 in Tegucigalpa

1. **Search civil registration first** — collection 2135627, filter to Distrito Central/Tegucigalpa, year 1889. The volumes covering this period are 100% indexed and searchable by name.
2. **If not found, search Catholic Church Records** — collection 1823595, searching by parent name (Micaela Salgado) and approximate year. Note the known indexing gap for Tegucigalpa cathedral circa 1879–1889; browsing images may be necessary.
3. **Check the legacy Baptisms index** (col. 1520634) as a pointer, but verify any hit in original images.
4. A nil result in all three collections is meaningful negative evidence for 1889 Tegucigalpa.

## Guillermo Salgado — Son of Micaela Salgado, Tegucigalpa, Honduras, Baptized 20 October 1889

**Tier: Probable | Form: Summary**

### Research Question

Did Micaela Salgado of Tegucigalpa, Honduras have a son named Guillermo baptized circa 1889, in addition to her known daughters born in 1874 and 1884?

### The Baptism Record

The primary evidence is a FamilySearch-indexed entry from the Honduras Catholic Church Records (diocesan registers, collection 1823595, covering 1633–1978). The index records a male child named Guillermo Salgado baptized on 20 October 1889 at San Miguel, Tegucigalpa, Francisco Morazán, Honduras, with the mother listed as "Micaila Salgado."^1 The parish officiant recorded this event at the time, making the underlying register an original source with primary information about the baptism. This conclusion relies on the derivative FamilySearch index rather than the original register, because the original parish image available at ark:/61903/1:2:9MV1-8XKD was not examined during this research phase. Accordingly, the tier is held at **probable** rather than proved; examination of the original image would allow advancement to proved and would confirm the exact form of the mother's name in the register.

### Identity of the Mother: Micaila = Micaela

The index spells the mother's name "Micaila" rather than "Micaela." This is a recognizable indexed variant — a transposition of vowels common when a handwritten register is transcribed. It does not indicate a different person. Three civil registration records for Tegucigalpa from 1884 and 1891 consistently use "Micaela Salgado" for a woman who was the mother of multiple children in the same city during the same period.^2,3 The combination of identical surname (Salgado), phonetically equivalent given name (Micaila/Micaela), Female sex, Tegucigalpa location, and consistent reproductive timeline — daughter Raimunda De Jesus baptized 1874, daughter Maria Norberta born 1884, son Guillermo baptized 1889, daughter Agueda born 1891 — makes it highly probable that the "Micaila Salgado" named in the 1889 record is the same individual as the Micaela Salgado (born c. 1854, Tegucigalpa) already established in the tree. No competing Micaela or Micaila Salgado in Tegucigalpa was identified in any record examined.

### Corroborating Evidence

Two civil registration records independently confirm Micaela Salgado's presence and active motherhood in Tegucigalpa in the years immediately bracketing 1889. The civil birth registration for Maria Norberta Salgado (registered 16 December 1884) names "Micaela Salgado" as mother.^2 The civil birth registration for Agueda Salgado (registered 27 February 1891) also names "Micaela Salgado" as mother.^3 Neither record mentions a son named Guillermo, but together they corroborate the subject's identity, location, and continuing role as a mother in Tegucigalpa across the period 1884–1891. The absence of a civil nacimiento for Guillermo is consistent with the known pattern of civil registration not universally capturing baptisms in Honduras in 1889.

### Conclusion

The evidence strongly suggests that Micaela Salgado of Tegucigalpa, Honduras had a son named Guillermo Salgado baptized on 20 October 1889 at San Miguel parish, Tegucigalpa, with no father recorded. Three sources from two independent record-creating systems — Catholic baptismal registers and civil birth registrations — converge to support this conclusion. The primary source (the 1889 baptism index entry) is derivative; consulting the original parish register image would be required to advance the conclusion to proved.

**Tier: Probable | Form: Summary**

### Research Question

Did Micaela Salgado of Tegucigalpa, Honduras have a son named Guillermo baptized circa 1889, in addition to her known daughters born in 1874 and 1884?

### The Baptism Record

The primary evidence is a FamilySearch-indexed entry from the Honduras Catholic Church Records (diocesan registers, collection 1823595, covering 1633–1978). The index records a male child named Guillermo Salgado baptized on 20 October 1889 at San Miguel, Tegucigalpa, Francisco Morazán, Honduras, with the mother listed as "Micaila Salgado."^1 The parish officiant recorded this event at the time, making the underlying register an original source with primary information about the baptism. This conclusion relies on the derivative FamilySearch index rather than the original register, because the original parish image available at ark:/61903/1:2:9MV1-8XKD was not examined during this research phase. Accordingly, the tier is held at **probable** rather than proved; examination of the original image would allow advancement to proved and would confirm the exact form of the mother's name in the register.

### Identity of the Mother: Micaila = Micaela

The index spells the mother's name "Micaila" rather than "Micaela." This is a recognizable indexed variant — a transposition of vowels common when a handwritten register is transcribed. It does not indicate a different person. Three civil registration records for Tegucigalpa from 1884 and 1891 consistently use "Micaela Salgado" for a woman who was the mother of multiple children in the same city during the same period.^2,3 The combination of identical surname (Salgado), phonetically equivalent given name (Micaila/Micaela), Female sex, Tegucigalpa location, and consistent reproductive timeline — daughter Raimunda De Jesus baptized 1874, daughter Maria Norberta born 1884, son Guillermo baptized 1889, daughter Agueda born 1891 — makes it highly probable that the "Micaila Salgado" named in the 1889 record is the same individual as the Micaela Salgado (born c. 1854, Tegucigalpa) already established in the tree. An automated algorithmic match score (same_person) returned a degenerate result (0.000007) due to an unresolvable tree ARK and was therefore set aside; the identification rests entirely on qualitative correlation as described above. A structured alternative-candidate assessment found no second Micaela or Micaila Salgado in Tegucigalpa in any record examined across this research plan (see hypothesis h_001).

### Corroborating Evidence

Two civil registration records independently confirm Micaela Salgado's presence and active motherhood in Tegucigalpa in the years immediately bracketing 1889. The civil birth registration for Maria Norberta Salgado (registered 16 December 1884) names "Micaela Salgado" as mother.^2 The civil birth registration for Agueda Salgado (registered 27 February 1891) also names "Micaela Salgado" as mother.^3 Neither record mentions a son named Guillermo, but together they corroborate the subject's identity, location, and continuing role as a mother in Tegucigalpa across the period 1884–1891. The absence of a civil nacimiento for Guillermo is consistent with the known pattern of civil registration not universally capturing baptisms in Honduras in 1889.

This proof addresses only whether Micaela Salgado had a son named Guillermo baptized in 1889. Two unresolved conflicts about Micaela's own parents (c_001: mother's identity; c_002: father's identity) remain in the research record. Those conflicts concern the generation above Micaela and do not affect the present conclusion.

### Conclusion

The evidence strongly suggests that Micaela Salgado of Tegucigalpa, Honduras had a son named Guillermo Salgado baptized on 20 October 1889 at San Miguel parish, Tegucigalpa, with no father recorded. Three sources from two independent record-creating systems — Catholic baptismal registers and civil birth registrations — converge to support this conclusion.
